live_issue.title: [v0.92.1][Observatory] Complete live Unity Observatory Runtime v3 integration
live_issue.body:
## Summary

Complete the Unity half of legacy WP-18A issue danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5837 as one independently executable consumer lane. Bind the existing Unity Observatory to the stable Runtime v3 API/WSS contract without absorbing HTML or shared cross-client integration.

## Goal

Make the approved Unity Observatory a truthful native Runtime v3 consumer with authenticated controls, explicit failure states, and retained Editor evidence.

## Required Outcome

The real Unity client reads the same Runtime state as HTML through one Runtime v3 transport adapter, performs only authorized controls, reconnects safely, validates the shared contract resource, and visibly distinguishes live, stale, offline, denied, incompatible, and transport-failure states.

## Deliverables

- Native Unity Runtime v3 client adapter.
- Existing approved shell bound to that adapter without visual redesign or a parallel Runtime v3 transport.
- Versioned Unity contract resource derived from the shared Runtime schema.
- Focused Unity client and compatibility tests.
- Staged native Editor validation with no player binary build.
- Positive and negative redaction, authorization, reconnect, command non-replay, and no-fixture-substitution proof.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `RuntimeV3Client.cs` consumes Runtime v3 public HTTPS snapshots, public WSS events, authenticated signed snapshot commands, local cursor continuity, correlation, and backpressure semantics.
- `UnityObservatoryShellController.cs` renders adapter state and does not retain an active parallel Runtime v3 transport path.
- `runtime-v3-contract.json` is derived from the shared contract and cannot become a Unity-only schema fork.
- The client performs only an externally signed `snapshot` control and exposes unavailable or denied actions without authority escalation.
- Public, operator, and reviewer projections do not expose private citizen state, signing material, certificate keys, or raw tokens.
- TLS/transport refusal, API/WSS version mismatch, stale/offline data, unavailable Runtime, malformed events, and backpressure are explicit states.
- Reconnect uses bounded backoff and local cursor deduplication without claiming protocol-level resume, duplicating applied events, or replaying commands.
- Native Editor proof exercises the real product adapter and Runtime path; fixtures and contract-only tests cannot satisfy live acceptance.
- Validation stages the project on FastWork, retains required Unity metadata and deterministic package-lock changes, and builds no player binary.
- One exact-head review has no unresolved actionable findings.

## Repo Inputs And Owned Paths

- Existing approved Unity Observatory project under `demos/v0.91.6/unity-observatory/`.
- `docs/api/runtime-v3/v1/observatory.openapi.json` and terminal WP-14 protocol evidence from danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5832.
- Runtime API/auth implementations are read-only inputs.
- Owned implementation paths are the adapter and `.meta`, existing shell controller, contract projection and `.meta`, Tests folder metadata and native test, deterministic `Packages/packages-lock.json`, and `adl/tools/validate_v092_unity_observatory_live.sh`, exactly as recorded in the typed SPP.

## Dependencies

- danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5820 Runtime launch/API terminal.
- danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5832 versioned HTTP/WSS protocol terminal.
- danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5836 reviewed first-birthday interaction surface is the input to observe; this issue supplies Unity/Observatory evidence required by #5836 publication and does not wait for #5836 terminal.
- Approved Unity 6000.5.1f1 Editor environment available for proof.

## Demo Expectations

Launch the staged approved Unity project against the exact Runtime candidate and retain native Editor evidence for live read, one authenticated signed snapshot request, denial, stale/offline behavior, reconnect, contract mismatch, and transport refusal. Do not build a player binary.

## Non-goals

- HTML code, styles, Playwright proof, or browser-specific behavior.
- Shared Runtime API/WSS implementation or the cross-client Guardian restart coordinator.
- Unity visual redesign, Runtime launch, protocol design, TLS authority, provider integration, or AWS work.
- Unity-only Runtime schemas, embedding fixtures as live state, or claiming protocol cursor resume that the WSS contract does not expose.

## Issue-Graph Notes

- Split from legacy parent danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5837.
- A separate HTML sibling owns all browser client paths and proof.
- The legacy parent retains shared compatibility reconciliation and cross-client restart/replay proof.
- Completion of this issue does not independently close or complete legacy #5837.

## Tooling Notes

Use the typed C-SDLC v2 lifecycle in the dedicated FastWork worktree. The implementation PR closes this new issue and records `Part of danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5837`; it must not close the legacy parent.

<!-- csdlc-github-operation:v092-wp18a-unity-split-from-legacy-5837-v2 -->
<!-- csdlc-github-operation:v092-wp18a-unity-5836-edge-reconcile-v1 -->


## Canonical migration routing

Current integration-parent authority is #340, migrated from legacy danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5837. Current birthday-demo authority is #256, migrated from legacy #5836. Historical legacy references above remain provenance only; future dependency, review, publication, and closeout coordination use #340 and #256.

<!-- csdlc-github-operation:issue-migration-routing-84-parent-340-v1 -->
<!-- csdlc-github-operation:v0921-wp01:f00977324d7bfbfcb17a04d1798d14eca9c99c6d6299a0ae21977f564b518251:existing-84:route -->
